properties.statement: Official wording (S1, Fefferman, Clay Mathematics Institute, PRIMARY-OFFICIAL): "we ask for a proof of one of the following four statements." Resolving the Clay problem therefore means proving any one of (A), (B), (C), (D); it does not require deciding the others. properties.name: The numbered conditions (1)–(11) of the official statement
properties.statement: As S1 (PRIMARY-OFFICIAL) names them: (1) the Navier–Stokes equations with viscosity ν > 0 and force f; (2) incompressibility (div u = 0); (3) the initial condition u(x,0) = u°(x); (4) a decay condition on u° and its derivatives; (5) a decay condition on f and its derivatives; (6) smoothness of p and u on R³ × [0,∞); (7) bounded energy (∫|u|² dx bounded for all t). (8)–(11) are the periodic (R³/Z³) counterparts used in (B) and (D); the packet does not quote their wording, so they are recorded by number only. Taken as given: these are the problem's definitions.

properties.statement: Constantin, Ignatova and Vicol, arXiv:2609.20803 (v1 2026-09-17, v2 2026-09-29), per its abstract. They describe OpenAI's construction as having (i) "the angular mean of the solution satisfies specific Type II bounds which are anisotropic" and (ii) "the solution is exactly axisymmetric in a collapsing core region". They prove: solutions with a real-analytic body force that satisfy (i) and (ii) "are in fact regular at the putative singular point". Consequence, quoted: "in the construction of [OpenAI], and in any construction with properties (i) and (ii) whose force remains bounded in C² up to the singular time, the force can neither vanish identically near the singular point, nor be real analytic in the space variables, locally uniformly in time." SCOPE: constructions with (i) and (ii) (and, for the consequence, a force bounded in C² up to the singular time). It does NOT dispute (C), which allows any smooth decaying force, and it does NOT address unforced blow-up outside properties (i) and (ii). Not refereed; abstract only.

properties.name: Lemma: if (A) fails, then (C) holds
properties.source: Designer's derivation from S1's wording of (A) and (C); not stated in any source in the packet
properties.statement: If not-(A), then (C). Reason: a counterexample to (A) is a smooth divergence-free u° satisfying (4) with f ≡ 0 for which no (p,u) satisfies (1), (2), (3), (6), (7) on R³ × [0,∞). The zero force is smooth on R³ × [0,∞) and satisfies the decay condition (5) (any bound of the form |derivatives of f| ≤ C·(decaying weight) holds for f ≡ 0). So the pair (u°, f ≡ 0) witnesses (C). The converse FAILS to follow: (C) may be witnessed only by a non-zero force, which says nothing about f ≡ 0. Hence (A) and (C) are compatible, and (C) does not decide (A). Written by the designer from S1's wording; the packet gives (5) only as 'a decay condition on f', so the step that f ≡ 0 satisfies it is general knowledge, put to the owner.

The converse does not follow: (D) with a non-zero force says nothing about (B). Written by the designer; the packet does not quote (8)–(11), so that f ≡ 0 meets (9) is assumed from general knowledge and put to the owner.

properties.name: SPECULATION 1 (not claimed by any source): the OpenAI-type blow-up survives switching the force off before the singular time
properties.source: Designer's speculation (proof-ladder trial speculative-links slot); not in any source
properties.statement: SPECULATION — written by the designer, claimed by NO source, NOT accepted. A finite-time singularity of the kind S5 attributes to OpenAI's construction (properties (i) anisotropic Type II bounds on the angular mean and (ii) exact axisymmetry in a collapsing core) can be produced with a smooth force satisfying (5) that is identically zero for all t ≥ T0, for some T0 before the singular time T*, with u(·,T0) satisfying (4). IF SHOWN it would give not-(A) (restart the clock at T0: unforced smooth data that breaks down). CIRCULAR: it is merely a special case of not-(A) — showing it IS showing not-(A) for one family of solutions — so it opens no route that not-(A) does not already name. Also, S5's consequence (abstract only) says that in constructions with (i), (ii) and a force bounded in C² up to T*, the force cannot vanish identically near the singular point — which, within that scope, stands against this speculation.

properties.name: SPECULATION 2 (not claimed by any source): no unforced solution can break down through an exactly axisymmetric collapsing core
properties.source: Designer's speculation (proof-ladder trial speculative-links slot); suggested by the scope of S5's abstract; not in any source
properties.statement: SPECULATION — written by the designer, claimed by NO source, NOT accepted. Every solution of the unforced 3-D Navier–Stokes equations (f ≡ 0) from smooth data satisfying (4) that is exactly axisymmetric in a collapsing core region is regular at any putative singular point — that is, S5's conclusion would hold for f ≡ 0 WITHOUT assuming its Type II bounds (i). IF SHOWN it would close one whole family of routes to not-(A) (including Speculation 1), yet leave (A) itself open, since breakdown without such a core would remain possible. NOT CIRCULAR: it is strictly weaker than (A) — (A) implies it (inf:a-implies-spec-2), but it does not imply (A) — and it is not a restatement of any of (A)–(D) or their negations.
